note: Code generated by internal/v2/norm TestWriteTwinArtifacts. DO NOT EDIT. These are SYNTHETIC inputs, unlike conformance/normalizer/*.json which is real corpus mail. They exist because the 7,002-message corpus contains zero examples of any of these classes — zero MIME parse failures, zero undecodable leaves, zero unknown charsets — and an untested class is where two implementations drift apart. Expectations are whatever the Go normalizer produces; the TypeScript twin must reproduce them byte for byte.

cases.name: qp-soft-break-lf

cases.name: qp-bad-hex-is-literal
cases.note: = not followed by two hex digits is a literal = (Go deviation 4)

cases.name: qp-eq-at-eof-dropped
cases.note: a trailing = at end of input is silently ignored (Go deviation 3)

cases.name: qp-eq-alone-at-eof-kills-leaf

cases.name: qp-ws-after-eq-still-soft

cases.name: qp-raw-high-byte-passes
cases.note: bytes >= 0x80 pass through unescaped (Go issue 22597)

cases.name: qp-control-byte-kills-leaf
cases.note: an unescaped control byte is fatal to the leaf

cases.name: qp-del-byte-kills-leaf

cases.name: qp-eq-line-alone
cases.note: a line that is only = followed by CRLF vanishes

cases.name: b64-embedded-space
cases.note: RFC 2045 permits whitespace; go-message rewrites space and tab to LF first

cases.name: b64-missing-padding-kills-leaf
cases.note: Go's decoder requires padding; the leaf is discarded, not salvaged

cases.name: b64-trailing-garbage-kills-leaf
cases.note: data after the padding is fatal

cases.name: b64-empty-payload
cases.note: an empty leaf is not recorded, so there is no text part

cases.name: cte-unknown-top-level-passes
cases.note: an unknown CTE on the TOP-LEVEL entity is tolerated and the body passes through undecoded

cases.name: charset-windows-1256
cases.note: the corpus's only non-UTF-8 charset

cases.name: charset-iso-8859-1-is-true-latin1
cases.note: ianaindex resolves iso-8859-1 to TRUE Latin-1, where WHATWG/TextDecoder would give windows-1252. The bytes 0x80 and 0x8D are the tell

cases.name: charset-iso8859-1-is-windows-1252
cases.note: the SAME encoding without the hyphen falls through to the WHATWG table and becomes windows-1252, where 0x8D is undefined

cases.name: charset-us-ascii-passes-high-bytes
cases.note: us-ascii is short-circuited by go-message: high bytes are NOT replaced at the charset layer, they reach stage 3 and become U+FFFD by the WHATWG rule

cases.name: charset-unknown-label-passes-through
cases.note: an unresolvable label leaves the body undecoded; stage 3 then substitutes

cases.name: mp-first-empty-html-skipped
cases.note: first NON-EMPTY, not first

cases.name: mp-no-final-boundary-raw-fallback
cases.note: the walk breaks before any leaf is collected, so the raw body is recorded rather than nothing

cases.name: mp-subpart-unknown-charset-raw-fallback
cases.note: ASYMMETRY: an unknown charset is tolerated on the top-level entity but ABORTS the walk on a sub-part, because NextPart returns it as an error

cases.name: mp-subpart-unknown-cte-raw-fallback
cases.note: same asymmetry for an unknown transfer encoding

cases.name: mp-bad-leaf-then-good-leaf
cases.note: an undecodable leaf is skipped without aborting the walk

cases.name: mp-cte-on-multipart-ignored
cases.note: RFC 2045 forbids it, real mailers do it anyway, go-message ignores it

cases.name: mp-part-defaults-to-text-plain
cases.note: a part with no Content-Type is text/plain with no charset

cases.name: ct-unparseable-skips-leaf
cases.note: a Content-Type mime.ParseMediaType rejects yields the RAW field as the media type, which matches neither text/html nor text/plain

cases.name: hdr-broken-first-line-raw
cases.note: the stage-1 raw fallback, with Subject and From recovered by the explicit scan

cases.name: hdr-leading-space-first-line-raw
cases.note: a header block may not begin with a folded line

cases.name: hdr-invalid-key-byte-raw
cases.note: a space inside a header key is invalid per RFC 5322 2.2

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-adjacent-words-join-bare
cases.note: adjacent encoded words join with NO separator; inserting a space breaks the ENBD last4 match

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-latin1-word
cases.note: mime.WordDecoder handles iso-8859-1 itself, as TRUE Latin-1

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-windows-1256-word
cases.note: an encoded word in a legacy charset goes through the same registry

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-us-ascii-high-byte
cases.note: the us-ascii branch of mime.WordDecoder emits ONE U+FFFD PER BYTE, not per maximal subpart

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-unknown-charset-kept-raw
cases.note: an undecodable word leaves the whole field at its raw value

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-body-only-alias-kept-raw
cases.note: THE TWO REGISTRIES DIFFER. ansi_x3.110-1983 is an ISO-8859-1 alias for a BODY (a go-message quirk) and is unknown to a WORD, because the word decoder is wired to htmlindex alone. Decoding it here would be a divergence

cases.name: hdr-rfc2047-ianaindex-only-name-kept-raw
cases.note: same shape: ibm037 resolves for a body and not for a word

cases.name: hdr-from-display-name-stripped
cases.note: From is reduced to the bare address

cases.name: hdr-from-unparseable-kept-raw
cases.note: a junk From is kept verbatim rather than dropped

cases.name: hdr-from-angle-addr-recovered
cases.note: the by-hand angle-addr recovery

cases.name: hdr-space-before-colon
cases.note: trailing spaces in a key appear in the wild and are trimmed

cases.name: hdr-lf-blank-beats-later-crlf-blank
cases.note: the body starts at whichever blank line comes FIRST

cases.name: hdr-raw-8bit-utf8-subject
cases.note: a Subject carrying raw UTF-8 with no RFC 2047 wrapper. Go's header value IS bytes, so this needs no decoding step at all; a twin that turned header bytes into text too early would emit one code point per byte

cases.name: hdr-raw-8bit-nbsp-padding
cases.note: the header trim is over RUNES: the two-byte encoding of U+00A0 is trimmed, and the value keeps its interior spacing

cases.name: html-entities-single-pass
cases.note: &lt; must become < and STOP; a chain of six replaces would produce <

cases.name: html-nbsp-collapses
cases.note: U+00A0 is in the collapse set, so it never survives to the trim

cases.name: trim-set-keeps-hair-space
cases.note: U+200A is NOT in the explicit trim set: a line of hair spaces survives

cases.name: trim-set-drops-feff-line
cases.note: U+FEFF IS in the explicit trim set: a lone BOM line is dropped

cases.name: trim-set-keeps-narrow-nbsp
cases.note: U+202F is not in the set either, unlike Go's TrimSpace

cases.name: trim-set-keeps-next-line
cases.note: U+0085 is trimmed by Go's TrimSpace and not by this contract

cases.name: plain-part-is-not-html-stripped
cases.note: a text/plain leaf skips stage 5 entirely, so markup survives

cases.name: fwd-quoted-recovers-nothing
cases.note: the shape 50 of the corpus's 56 forwards have: the marker is unquoted, every header line is > quoted, so nothing is recovered and the body is unchanged

cases.name: fwd-date-iphone-seconds-ampm-unparsed
cases.note: K2: the four closed layouts cover seconds OR AM/PM, never both, so this dates to the arrival time

cases.name: fwd-date-narrow-nbsp-before-ampm
cases.note: Apple Mail inserts U+202F before AM/PM on recent OSes

cases.name: fwd-marker-but-no-headers
cases.note: Forwarded is true because a MARKER was found, not because headers were recovered

cases.name: fwd-date-zone-token-is-stripped
cases.note: MUTATION GUARD: without the retry that drops the final space-delimited token, this trailing zone name makes the whole value unparseable and the transaction silently dates to its arrival time

cases.name: fwd-date-iso8601-is-not-a-layout
cases.note: MUTATION GUARD: Date.parse accepts this and the four closed layouts do not. A twin that reached for Date.parse would date the transaction from the body where Go dates it from arrival

cases.name: fwd-date-no-at-keyword-is-not-a-layout
cases.note: MUTATION GUARD: Date.parse accepts "Jul 24, 2026 4:11 PM" in the LOCAL zone; every layout here requires the literal " at "

cases.name: html-block-tag-pass-precedes-generic-rule
cases.note: MUTATION GUARD: on well-formed HTML the five block tags are inert, because the generic tag rule yields the same newline. They are only observable on MALFORMED markup, where the generic rule swallows the block tag as part of a longer pseudo-tag
